title.narrative: Education for the Poor - Financial Crisis Response Project

description.narrative: The financial and economic crisis has forced the Government of Mongolia (the Government) to embark on a process of fiscal adjustment. This is primarily centered around expenditure restraint in view of the dramatic worsening of prices of key exports, dwindling international reserves, and increased pressures on its currency. The Government is acutely aware of the pressure the current global crisis is placing on Mongolia's most vulnerable citizens and has therefore asked the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to help safeguard achievements in the education sector and to mitigate any negative impact of the crisis on the poor. The Project will support (i) financing of meals at preschools for children ages 2-5 to protect access to preschools for poor children; (ii) continuation of the targeted provision of textbooks to secondary school students from poor families; (iii) provision of block grants to schools in need of operation and maintenance funds; and (iv) capacity building at the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science (MECS) in financial management, budgeting, and monitoring and evaluation to enable MECS to better deal with budget constraints. The Project is in line with the $229.2 million standby arrangement of the International Monetary Fund for Mongolia that requires the Government to maintain a tight fiscal policy to restore fiscal sustainability, and advocates donor support to mitigate the impact of the fiscal adjustment on the poor. The Project complements the Social Sectors Support Program approved in June 2009 that will support a comprehensive overhaul of the existing system of social transfer programs to better target these programs to the very poor while conserving fiscal resources. The Social Sectors Support Program will introduce proxy means testing (PMT) to improve targeting of the provision of free textbooks and the Project will help MECS operationalize PMT and enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of education service delivery. The Project is a sector intervention that will support the Government in addressing short-term financing needs and continuing longer-term policy reform in the education sector.

description.narrative: Education system financing and efficiency improved.

MECS implements PMT as a targeting methodology for free textbook provision Progress/Status: The PMT was initially piloted in three schools and preliminary analysis of data on school children from schools, Khoroo (smallest administrative units), and PMT revealed that the data from the PMT alone were inadequate for the purpose of targeting poor students for the free textbook program as it was developed by the Ministry of Population Development and Social Protection for a different purpose under the ADB-financed Food and Nutrition Social Welfare Project. Hence, a different set of criteria including data on poor children derived from the PMT were adopted to target students for the free textbook program. Data Source: MECS annual reports generated through the EMIS Base year: 2010 Baseline value: N

MECS reviews budgeting formula with a view to gradually increase recurrent budget allocations starting in SY 2012/13 Progress/Status: The project provided adequate budgets to finance textbooks, meals at preschools, and grants to support block grant activities and to build capacity of education personnel at all levels to further enhance efficiency of the education system. Targets for all activities—free textbooks, free meals for preschools, number of schools receiving block grants, and number of participants attending capacity building programs— met or exceeded the targets with savings of 2.1 million which was used for additional activities resulting in more beneficiaries of the project. Base year: 2010 Baseline value: N

Preschool meal provision is ensured in SY2009/10 and SY2010/11, and the delivery mechanism is improved Progress/Status: From school year 2010/11, the education budget has started to cover free meal program nationwide. Base year: 2010 Baseline value: N
